overview.definition: An electronic, programmable device that accepts raw data as input, processes it according to stored instructions (software), produces meaningful information as output, and stores results for future use.
overview.gigo_principle: Garbage In, Garbage Out (GIGO): If invalid data is input into a computer, the resulting output will inevitably be invalid.

characteristics.description: Executes millions to billions of instructions per second (measured in MIPS, BIPS, or GHz clock cycles).
High degree of calculation precision with zero calculation fatigue or computational error unless programmed wrongly.
Free from monotony, tiredness, or lack of concentration; operates continuously for months without loss of accuracy.
Can perform diverse tasks simultaneously from core banking transactions to digital graphics.
Stores vast volumes of data permanently in secondary storage (terabytes to petabytes).
Cannot think, judge, or feel autonomously without explicit human algorithmic programming.

fathers_of_computing.title: Father of the Computer
fathers_of_computing.contribution: Invented Difference Engine (1822) and Analytical Engine (1837), which introduced input, processing, memory (store), control, and output.

fathers_of_computing.title: First Computer Programmer
fathers_of_computing.contribution: Wrote the first algorithm intended to be executed on Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine.

fathers_of_computing.title: Father of Modern Computer Science & AI
fathers_of_computing.contribution: Formulated Turing Machine concept, Turing Test for AI, and designed Bombe machine to crack Enigma code.

fathers_of_computing.title: Architect of Stored-Program Architecture
fathers_of_computing.contribution: Pioneered Von Neumann Architecture (1945), where data and program instructions share common memory.

generations.language: Machine Language (0s and 1s) and Assembly Language
generations.characteristics: Enormous physical size, consumed massive electricity, generated excessive heat, frequent hardware burnouts.
examples: ENIAC (Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer - First general-purpose electronic computer, built by Eckert & Mauchly)
UNIVAC I (Universal Automatic Computer - First commercial computer)
generations.exam_fact: ENIAC was developed at the University of Pennsylvania by J. Presper Eckert and John Mauchly.

generations.switching_device: Transistors (invented in 1947 at Bell Labs by John Bardeen, Walter Brattain, and William Shockley)
generations.memory_storage: Magnetic Core Memory, Magnetic Tape and Disks
generations.language: High-Level Languages emerged: FORTRAN (Formula Translation - 1957, by John Backus) and COBOL (Common Business Oriented Language - 1959, led by Grace Hopper)
generations.characteristics: Smaller, faster, cheaper, more energy-efficient and reliable than vacuum tubes.
generations.exam_fact: Transistors replaced vacuum tubes; FORTRAN and COBOL were introduced in this generation.

generations.switching_device: Integrated Circuits (ICs) - Small Scale Integration (SSI) & Medium Scale Integration (MSI), invented in 1958 by Jack Kilby and Robert Noyce
generations.memory_storage: Magnetic Core replaced gradually by Semiconductor RAM
generations.language: Advanced High-Level Languages: BASIC, PASCAL, PL/1
generations.characteristics: Time-sharing Operating Systems introduced, keyboards and monitors replaced punched cards.
generations.exam_fact: Silicon chips / Integrated Circuits (ICs) were invented by Jack Kilby.

generations.switching_device: Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) & Microprocessors (Intel 4004 - world's first single-chip 4-bit microprocessor, 1971 by Ted Hoff & Federico Faggin)
generations.memory_storage: Semiconductor Semiconductor RAM/ROM, Hard Disks, Optical Disks
generations.characteristics: Birth of Personal Computers (PCs), Graphical User Interface (GUI), Internet, distributed computing.
examples: CRAY-1 (First commercially successful Supercomputer by Seymour Cray, 1976)
generations.exam_fact: Intel 4004 was the world's first commercial microprocessor; CRAY-1 was developed by Seymour Cray ('Father of Supercomputing').

generations.switching_device: Ultra Large Scale Integration (ULSI), Quantum computing chips, and Optical/Photonic chips
generations.memory_storage: High-density SSDs (NVMe), Cloud distributed storage, Holographic memory
generations.language: Natural Language Processing (NLP), Python, R, AI frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow)
generations.characteristics: Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning, Voice Recognition, Parallel Processing, Quantum Supremacy.
generations.exam_fact: Fifth generation computers focus on AI, parallel processing, and natural language understanding.

by_working_principle.definition: Operates on continuous physical variables such as voltage, pressure, temperature, and current. Used in scientific measurement and speedometers.
by_working_principle.example: Mercury thermometer, mechanical speedometer, operational amplifiers.

by_working_principle.definition: Processes data in discrete binary digits (0 and 1). High precision, general purpose, handles arithmetic and logical calculations.
by_working_principle.example: Laptops, smartphones, bank ATM kiosks, desktops.

by_working_principle.definition: Combines features of both Analog (speed of continuous data measurement) and Digital (precision of numerical calculation).
by_working_principle.example: Intensive Care Unit (ICU) patient heart monitors, petrol pump fuel meters, flight simulators.

by_size_and_capability.definition: Most powerful, fastest, and most expensive computers designed for massive mathematical processing and scientific simulations.
by_size_and_capability.speed_unit: FLOPS (Floating Point Operations Per Second: PetaFLOPS, ExaFLOPS)
by_size_and_capability.father: Seymour Cray (Father of Supercomputing). Dr. Vijay Bhatkar is the Father of Indian Supercomputing (PARAM 8000 in 1991).
by_size_and_capability.applications: Weather forecasting, nuclear weapon simulations, quantum mechanics, drug discovery.
by_size_and_capability.examples: Frontier (USA - world's first verified Exascale supercomputer), Fugaku (Japan), PARAM Siddhi-AI (India), AIRAWAT (India).

by_size_and_capability.definition: High-performance enterprise computers designed to support thousands of concurrent users and process massive transactional databases with 99.999% uptime.
by_size_and_capability.applications: Core Banking Solution (CBS) systems at RBI/SBI, insurance claims, airline ticket reservations, census databases.

by_size_and_capability.definition: Medium-sized multi-user computer lying between mainframes and microcomputers. Can support 4 to 200 users simultaneously.
by_size_and_capability.applications: Departmental servers, university research labs, manufacturing control.

by_size_and_capability.definition: Single-user computer powered by a single microprocessor chip. Most ubiquitous category.
Specialized computer system with a dedicated function embedded within a larger mechanical or electrical system. Runs on a microcontroller or SoC with fixed firmware in ROM.
by_size_and_capability.applications: ATM machines, Point of Sale (POS) terminals, washing machines, car engine ECUs, smart TVs.
by_size_and_capability.examples: ATM card reader controller, digital microwave timer.
